# Corvint MCP servers

Status: experimental; protocol `2026-07-28` (and `2025-11-25` with `--protocol-version 2025-11-25`); local stdio only.

Corvint serves its MCP tools from two local, read-only stdio servers (owner decision R30, the
MCP tool table of [`docs/specs/mcp-tool-table-v1.md`](specs/mcp-tool-table-v1.md)):

- `corvint mcp` serves the testing and flow-report tools.
- `corvint-docs mcp` serves the documentation tools and works with only the documentation
  binaries installed.

Neither serves a Tasks tool: Corvint Tasks is used through its command line (owner decision R17).
Every tool, its server, inputs, output profile, typed errors and command-line equivalent below comes
from one authored table, `internal/capcatalog/mcp.go`; a drift test fails when a server
registers a tool the table does not list, or the table lists one the server does not register. The
servers expose no repository source, prompts, writes, test execution, updates, telemetry, HTTP or
network listener. The wire contract is
[`docs/specs/mcp-server-2026-07-28-v0.md`](specs/mcp-server-2026-07-28-v0.md).

## Configure a client

Configure an MCP client to own the server as a child process, with absolute paths and no shell:

```json
{
  "command": "/absolute/path/to/corvint",
  "args": ["mcp", "--root", "/absolute/path/to/repository", "--tool-profile", "flows,test-evidence,affected"],
  "transport": "stdio"
}
```

```json
{
  "command": "/absolute/path/to/corvint-docs",
  "args": ["mcp", "--root", "/absolute/path/to/repository", "--corpus-artifact", "corpus.json"],
  "transport": "stdio"
}
```

Do not configure a URL, port, environment credential or writable working directory as authority.
One process is bound to its declared roots for its whole lifetime; request arguments cannot switch
them. Each server's `--help` documents every option, including `--root ALIAS=ROOT`
for several roots, `--workspace FILE` and `--follow-ref REF`.

Tool names follow one convention, `corvint.<area>_<verb>` with exactly one dot; a renamed tool
lists its earlier names under Replaces. A call to a tool a server does not list, including a removed
one, is the unknown-tool error `-32602`.

## Results and errors

Successful calls return the complete canonical receipt as one text content block, framed by the
untrusted-data envelope, and, except for the flow tools whose repository-authored text travels only
inside the envelope, as the identical parsed `structuredContent`. `READY` means the bounded
operation returned its native receipt; it does not mean Corvint proved the requested proposition.
`ABSTAINED`, `UNKNOWN`, `NOT_OBSERVED`, exclusions, mixed-worktree state and unsupported
intent are results, not missing fields. Source and diff bodies are never returned. Every tool lists
the typed tool errors `server-busy` and `cancelled` beside its own.

An impact receipt with native state `OUT_OF_SCOPE` is retained while its bridge wrapper says
`ABSTAINED`/`NOT_OBSERVED` with reason `OUT_OF_SCOPE`; this preserves the exclusion evidence.
Unsupported and output-budget abstentions have a null native receipt.

| Code/state | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `-32700` | Invalid, duplicate-key, too-deep, or over-limit JSON frame | Fix framing; the server never echoes rejected input |
| `-32600` | Invalid JSON-RPC request envelope | Send JSON-RPC `2.0`, a string/integer ID, method, and object params |
| `-32601` | Unknown, removed legacy, or unadvertised request method | Re-run `server/discover`; do not assume an older MCP surface |
| `-32602` | Missing request metadata, invalid cursor, unknown tool, or invalid closed arguments | Correct the request; no repository operation ran |
| `-32022` | Unsupported protocol version | Retry only with one of the returned `supported` versions |
| `-32603` | Sanitized unexpected server failure | Treat the operation as unobserved; inspect local process health |
| `ABSTAINED` | Corvint could not safely produce the requested bounded receipt | Preserve the receipt's reason and gaps; widen through an explicit supported operation |

A tool error with `code` `repository-probe-timeout` means the repository probe outlasted its own
bound while the request was still live; retrying on a quieter host is reasonable (`MCPV0-038`).
`repository-unavailable` remains every other repository refusal. Starting `corvint mcp` with
`--error-profile reason-class` makes every tool error `corvint-mcp-tool-error/1`, which adds a
required `reasonClass` from a closed set (`MCPV0-027..028`); read an unknown value as
`unclassified`.

Errors never include request bodies, repository paths, task text, environment values, Git output,
Corvint output, or secrets. stdout is exclusively MCP; startup and fatal transport diagnostics use
sanitized stderr.

## `corvint mcp`: testing and flow reports

Start it with `corvint mcp --root ABSOLUTE_ROOT`. Without `--tool-profile` it lists
`corvint.help`, `corvint.impact` and `corvint.status`; `--tool-profile LIST` adds the
comma list of the profile `flows` and the groups `test-evidence` and `affected`. The
`docs` and `corpus` groups moved to `corvint-docs mcp`: asking `corvint mcp` for either
exits 2 before any MCP byte with a typed `profile-moved` reason naming `corvint-docs mcp`,
and the removed `test-validity` group exits 2 the same way. The deprecated `corvint-mcp`
binary serves the same tools except `corvint.affected`, whose planner only the `corvint`
binary holds.

`corvint.affected` answers with the exact `affected-summary/1` bytes `corvint affected --summary`
prints, or, where the command line would exit 2, a successful select-all answer naming its reason:
a `CORVINT_SELECTION` kill switch (MTT-V1-008) or a stale binary (MTT-V1-011). One planner runs
at a time per root; a verdict too large for one message is the tool error `verdict-oversized`.

| Tool | Availability | Opt-in | Description | Same answer on the command line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `corvint.affected` | experimental | `--tool-profile affected` | Which tests a change requires: the affected-summary/1 verdict for a base or for the dirty worktree, or a select-all answer with its reason | `corvint affected --summary [--base REV]` |
| `corvint.flows.coverage` | experimental | `--tool-profile flows` | Complete accepted flow variation coverage, bound to immutable bytes; the page verdict covers the full inventory | `corvint-docs flows coverage` |
| `corvint.flows.gaps` | experimental | `--tool-profile flows` | Flows at HEAD without passing test evidence and, with a provider, the E2E tests no flow variation links | `corvint-docs flows gaps` |
| `corvint.flows.impact` | experimental | `--tool-profile flows` | The flows the base..HEAD changed paths reach through links and the impact graph | `corvint-docs flows impact` |
| `corvint.flows.map` | experimental | `--tool-profile flows` | Flow intents at HEAD with their links and test evidence, or the flows one path or test key reaches | `corvint-docs flows map` |
| `corvint.flows.navigate` | experimental | `--tool-profile flows` | The navigation map of the flow intents, or the ordered packet that reaches one goal flow with each step above maxEffect marked requires-grant | `corvint-docs flows navigate` |
| `corvint.flows.status` | experimental | `--tool-profile flows` | Each flow at HEAD, its variations, attached tests and the last recorded result of each, optionally only the flows a change reaches | `corvint-docs flows status` |
| `corvint.help` | experimental | default | Corvint's agent guide, one command's catalog entry, or the full command catalog, read from the binary; listed on both servers | `corvint help guide \| corvint help --json COMMAND \| corvint help --json` |
| `corvint.impact` | experimental | default | Revision-bound impact evidence for Go, Ruby, JavaScript and TypeScript paths, without source bodies | `corvint impact --language-profile non-go-syntax-v0 --limit N PATH...` |
| `corvint.status` | experimental | default | Exact commit, tree, worktree state and a privacy-preserving dirty-path digest of the served root | none |
| `corvint.test_evidence` | preview | `--tool-profile test-evidence` | Retained test evidence for a path, a test, or a test's explanation against a base, read-only | `corvint test-evidence` |

### `corvint.affected`

Which tests a change requires: the affected-summary/1 verdict for a base or for the dirty worktree, or a select-all answer with its reason.

- Input schema: `internal/mcp/toolgroup/affected.go`
- Input `base`: Optional base revision; with it the plan is base..HEAD plus the dirty worktree, without it the dirty worktree alone.
- Output profile: `affected-summary/1`
- Tool errors: `cancelled`, `server-busy`, `affected-failed`, `invalid-root`, `not-served`, `verdict-oversized`
- Note: a planner refusal carries the CLI's own error code; an unknown CORVINT_SELECTION value and a stale binary select all tests where the CLI exits 2 (MTT-V1-008, MTT-V1-011)

### `corvint.flows.coverage`

Complete accepted flow variation coverage, bound to immutable bytes; the page verdict covers the full inventory.

- Input schema: `internal/mcp/bridge/flows.go`
- Input `denominator`: Repository-relative accepted variation denominator file.
- Input `limit`: Most rows in this page, 1 to 100.
- Input `offset`: Rows to skip before this page.
- Input `receipts`: Repository-relative run receipts file.
- Output profile: `application-flow-coverage/1`
- Tool errors: `cancelled`, `server-busy`, `flows-refused`, `internal-error`, `repository-unavailable`, `corvint-envelope-terminator-collision`

### `corvint.flows.gaps`

Flows at HEAD without passing test evidence and, with a provider, the E2E tests no flow variation links.

- Input schema: `internal/mcp/bridge/flows.go`
- Input `evidence`: Repository-relative test evidence files to join to the flows.
- Input `flows`: Repository-relative directory holding the flow intent files.
- Input `provider`: Repository-relative E2E inventory provider file.
- Input `registry`: Repository-relative E2E test registry file.
- Output profile: `application-flow-gaps/1`
- Tool errors: `cancelled`, `server-busy`, `flows-refused`, `internal-error`, `repository-unavailable`, `corvint-envelope-terminator-collision`

Flow intents at HEAD with their links and test evidence, or the flows one path or test key reaches.

- Output profile: `corvint-mcp-bridge-result/0`

Exact commit, tree, worktree state and a privacy-preserving dirty-path digest of the served root.

- Input schema: `internal/mcp/bridge/bridge.go`
- Inputs: none
- Output profile: `corvint-mcp-bridge-result/0`
- Tool errors: `cancelled`, `server-busy`, `internal-error`, `repository-unavailable`, `corvint-envelope-terminator-collision`
- Note: no command prints this receipt; corvint status does not exist

### `corvint.test_evidence`

Retained test evidence for a path, a test, or a test's explanation against a base, read-only.

- Input schema: `internal/mcp/toolgroup/test_evidence.go`
- Input `base`: Base commit for explain.
- Input `explain`: Test whose selection to explain against base.
- Input `index`: Optional repository-relative test inventory file.
- Input `lines`: Optional START:END line range within path.
- Input `path`: Repository-relative path whose tests to read.
- Input `revision`: Commit to read at; default HEAD.
- Input `test`: Test whose dependencies to read.
- Output profile: `corvint-test-evidence-query/1`
- Tool errors: `cancelled`, `server-busy`, `internal-error`, `invalid-root`

## `corvint-docs mcp`: documentation

Start it with `corvint-docs mcp --root ABSOLUTE_ROOT [--corpus-artifact PATH]`. It always lists
`corvint.help`, `corvint.docs_draft`, `corvint.docs_consume` and every corpus tool.
`--corpus-artifact PATH` binds the corpus artifact, a path relative to the root; an artifact
that opens at startup lists exactly the tools it declares. Without it, or while the artifact cannot
be opened, each corpus call answers the tool error `corpus-refused` naming the fix. The draft
and consume tools run the `corvint-docs` executable's `docs-tool` verb. The deprecated
`corvint-docs-mcp` binary still serves `corvint.help`, `corvint.docs_draft` and
`corvint.docs_consume` until its removal is decided.

| Tool | Availability | Opt-in | Description | Same answer on the command line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `corvint.docs_claims` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Claims about a path, claims ranked by text, or supplied status claims by state, qualifier and run, filterable by claim kind | `corvint-docs docs corpus claims --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_concept` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | One concept's record, found by name | `corvint-docs docs corpus concept --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_consume` | experimental | default | Recheck a draft's exact bytes against source and return the bounded task match | `corvint-docs docs consume --source PATH --package DIR --task TEXT --draft FILE` |
| `corvint.docs_coverage` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Documentation coverage counts per outcome | `corvint-docs docs corpus coverage --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_dependencies` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | What one subject depends on | `corvint-docs docs corpus dependencies --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_draft` | experimental | default | A source-pinned documentation draft of a module directory; dry_run previews an untracked or inline owner as NOT_ADMISSIBLE | `corvint-docs docs draft --source PATH --package DIR` |
| `corvint.docs_find_related` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Subjects related to one subject | `corvint-docs docs corpus related --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_flow` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | One documented flow, its sections and records | `corvint-docs docs corpus flow --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_gaps` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Producer gap claims, optionally for one subject or gap kind | `corvint-docs docs corpus gaps --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_get` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | One subject and its links, by id or legacy case id | `corvint-docs docs corpus get --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_get_journey` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | One user journey of a subject | `corvint-docs docs corpus journey --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_get_stability` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Stability records of one subject | `corvint-docs docs corpus stability --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_how` | planned | default | Answer a how-to question from the application map | `corvint-docs how --json` |
| `corvint.docs_info` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | The corpus header, revision and capabilities | `corvint-docs docs corpus info --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_intent` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Intent records of one subject, or every intent comparison | `corvint-docs docs corpus intent --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_inventory` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | A page of the corpus inventory of a schema /2 artifact | `corvint-docs docs corpus inventory --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_locate` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Where a path is documented, or module and symbol subjects ranked by a query, with line anchors | `corvint-docs docs corpus locate --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_navigation` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Navigation structure of one flow, or of the flows a query selects by name or linked test | `corvint-docs docs corpus navigation --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_recommend_tests` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Tests the corpus links to a path and the subjects documenting it | `corvint-docs docs corpus recommend-tests --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_search` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Search the corpus: a compact receipt by default, the full one on request | `corvint-docs docs corpus search --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_trace` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Relations walked from one subject to a depth | `corvint-docs docs corpus trace --artifact PATH` |
| `corvint.docs_validate` | experimental | `--corpus-artifact PATH` | Validation of the corpus artifact itself | `corvint-docs docs corpus validate --artifact PATH` |

### `corvint.docs_claims`

Claims about a path, claims ranked by text, or supplied status claims by state, qualifier and run, filterable by claim kind.

- Input schema: `internal/mcp/corpusbridge/corpusbridge.go`
- Input `caller_revision`: Optional full commit id the caller works at; the receipt says whether the corpus was built at it.
- Input `limit`: Most records to return in this page, 1 to the corpus result bound.
- Input `offset`: Records to skip before this page, for a schema /2 artifact.
- Input `retirement`: Which retired records to include: the corpus retirement filter.
- Input `exclude_kind`: Claim kind, or list of kinds, to leave out.
- Input `kind`: Claim kind, or list of kinds, to keep.
- Input `path`: One repository path or symbol to look up; give path or paths, not both.
- Input `paths`: A batch of repository paths or symbols to look up; give path or paths, not both.
- Input `qualifier`: Supplied status qualifier to filter by.
- Input `query`: Claim text to rank against, in place of path or paths.
- Input `run`: Supplied status run id to filter by.
- Input `state`: Supplied status state to filter by.
- Output profile: `corvint-corpus-receipt/2`
- Tool errors: `cancelled`, `server-busy`, `corpus-input-unavailable`, `corpus-refused`, `corpus-unavailable`, `deadline-exceeded`, `internal-error`, `corvint-envelope-terminator-collision`

## `corvint-test-validity-mcp`: retiring

`corvint.test_validity` left `corvint mcp` with the G24 batch (owner decision M12). Until
its removal batch takes the `corvint-test-validity-mcp` binary off the release list
(MTT-V1-010), that binary is the only server that answers it.

| Tool | Availability | Opt-in | Description | Same answer on the command line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `corvint.test_validity` | deprecated | default | Five-axis projection of retained test evidence | `corvint test-validity` |

### `corvint.test_validity`

Five-axis projection of retained test evidence.

- Input schema: `internal/mcp/testvaliditybridge/testvaliditybridge.go`
- Input `discover`: Discover retained receipts instead of naming one.
- Input `receipt`: Retained test receipt to project.
- Output profile: `corvint-mcp-test-validity-result/0`
- Tool errors: `cancelled`, `server-busy`, `internal-error`, `repository-unavailable`
- Note: removed from corvint mcp with the G24 batch (M12); served only by the retiring corvint-test-validity-mcp binary until its removal batch (MTT-V1-010)

## No MCP tool

These answers are deliberately served only by a command line.

| Answer | Command | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Corvint Tasks is used through its command line; neither server serves a Tasks tool | `corvint-tasks` | no Tasks MCP server or tool ships in 1.0 (owner decision R17, MTT-V1-006) |

## Limits and lifecycle

- One UTF-8 JSON object per LF-delimited input line; one JSON object per output line.
- Input and output JSON are each at most 1,048,576 bytes before LF; nesting depth is at most 64.
- A valid `notifications/cancelled` cancels only its matching in-flight request. Clean EOF stops
  admission and drains admitted responses; SIGINT, SIGTERM and transport failure cancel owned work.
- Tool listing is deterministic and one page; tool receipts are never paged or silently truncated.
- Client-advertised roots are ignored. Repository authority is exclusively the startup roots.

## Privacy and authority

Corvint reads local Git and repository evidence under the configured roots. It does not fetch or
make network requests. Receipts may contain repository-relative paths and content identities even
though source bodies are omitted; treat them as sensitive local metadata. Every Git runner a server
uses is pinned to one absolute start-time Git executable (`MCPV0-016`); a Git binary placed on
PATH after start never runs. Never infer correctness, exhaustive coverage, or a clean worktree from
a successful transport response.

## Verification status

The compiled-process black-box suite under `conformance/mcp-2026-07-28` and the drift, table
and parity tests of MTT-V1 are the local evidence. Official 2026-07-28 MCP conformance remains
`NOT_RUN`: the official server runner requires a Streamable HTTP URL and offers no stdio
target, while these servers deliberately expose no listener. Do not promote this surface from
experimental until the owning spec's acceptance matrix passes. Disable or remove the child-process
configuration to roll back; the servers create no repository, trace, database, network, or
migration state.
